analysis.title: GS US TMT.. what a week ..
key_insights: NDX closed down ~5% last week and is on a 4-week losing streak. SOX fell about 28% over 22 days, one of its largest rolling 1-month drawdowns in history.
Earnings were a side-show last week. Focus was on risk reductions and recalibrating datacenter build expectations after last Tuesday's mid-term election.

Flow data showed record put volumes, elevated ETF volumes, signs of 'panic' in vol metrics, elevated sell skews and oversold conditions. The desk says this arguably sets up technical relief as vol normalizes and risk appetite rebases.

By the end of the week, investor conversations shifted to what is priced in for y/y capex (or GW) builds. The desk says this is more an exercise for 2028+ than 2027, and asks whether too much of a 2028+ slowdown is already priced in.

Sentiment is described as a very tough market. Strong bottom-up datapoints (memory pricing, compute pricing, supply/demand visibility, 3Q earnings) sit against weak price action. AI/Semis have been in a rolling bear market since summer, now about 40% off the highs.
Portfolio managers face tension managing long/short books in Semis, because the short leg is tricky when everything is compressed. Diversifying elsewhere is hard given re-ratings outside Semis/Tech.
Under-the-hood progress over the last month: strong earnings, oil and rates relief, lowered expectations, and positioning and valuation resets.
DRAM names (MU, Hynix, Samsung) trade at 2-3x forward P/E while spot prices remain near highs. The desk frames whether those multiples are interesting or risky as an open debate.
Analog semis showed relative resilience until late last week, while industrials saw outflows and drawdowns (CAT vs TXN charted).
The valuation premium of S&P staples to SPX is at its highest in 10+ years. The consumer staples index trades at about 2x the 24-month forward multiple of the semiconductor index.
Info Tech again paced the market higher with best-in-class 3Q earnings results, despite price action.
Week ahead is lighter on earnings (AMAT, CSCO, TTWO, IFX, SE) with analyst days and macro data (CPI, PPI). The desk calls it a 'day at a time' market with less benefit of the doubt.

Top client inbounds: what inning of the AI drawdown, any turn before year-end, durable non-AI names (ABNB, FWONK, SPHR, LYV, TTWO, DIS), software high-flyers NET and DDOG, semis preferences post drawdown, APP and U moves, OTAs into 2027 (BKNG/EXPE vs ABNB), and what to do with Memory.

sector_views.rationale: Sector is down about 28% in a month and about 40% off highs. Desk says flow extremes could set up technical relief, but notes unknowns and choppier two-way datapoints ahead.
Valuation premium to SPX is the highest in 10+ years, and the desk flags that investors may start to look at names up too much.
